N-ary union and square-union stem audit

Saved source: sources/SomervilleMath.glyphspackage. No glyph edits performed.

Scope: the 16 matching master/High layers of the active bowls, their plain and serif cap assemblies, both cap glyphs, and 1,344 stored outline layers across 84 ssty1/ssty2 glyphs. Excludes inactive backup layers and the unused legacy _smart.naryunion.bowel. This is a saved-source geometry audit, not a live Glyphs or exported-font audit. Interpolated component-only size glyphs are not independently rendered. Small discrepancies are reported, including likely rounding. Position differences between round and square glyphs are review items, not proof of a design error.

U = union; S = square union; UC/SC = plain cap assemblies; US/SS = serif cap assemblies. All numbers are font units. Stem widths are measured horizontally. Stem anchor centring means the midpoint of the two stem edges at the upper join. Positive deltas mean rightward/upward. Main source-layer “High” means smart height 100. Generated STYA/STYB 1200 layers retain their full source names.

Source issues · Centre anchors and spacing · Round/square placement · All script-size findings

Source-layer anchor, stem and cap-join findings

All 16 source pairs have equal left/right widths at the upper join, and equal upper-join widths between U and S. The tapered shaft below is the exception to matching widths throughout the stem. All cap stem-foot widths match their bowl stem widths; the cap-join faults are placement errors.

Stored script-size outlines: complete discrepancy table

1,344 layers checked. 6497 individual check flags; a layer can have several flags. Anchor x/y differences of up to 1 unit are consistent with rounded outlines and fractional stored anchors. They are included without silently applying a rounding tolerance. The 374 left/right width differences include 373 of 1 unit and one of 2 units. The 140 U/S width comparisons include 139 with a maximum side difference of 1 unit and one of 2 units. Cap-foot checks compare the stored contour edges directly.
